expectations.text: SPEC_ESTABLISHED: A requirements spec (Mission + at least one Goal + Premises + Constraints) was built before any attack and recorded in the trace/spec output.
expectations.evidence: spec.md: Mission + G1–G5 + P1–P4 + CH1–CH5 + CS1–CS4; trace Step 1 grounded the spec by executing the original (surfaced the off-by-one and silent empties).

expectations.text: AR_INFERRED_ISOLATED: Anti-requirements were inferred via an isolated sub-agent given ONLY the requirements — or, if sub-agents were unavailable, the degradation is explicitly marked (NO-AR-DEGRADED).
expectations.evidence: ar_inferrer_prompt.txt is requirements-only; ar_list.md has 15 ARs; trace records the isolated sub-agent agentId and the Pipeline Completeness Gate before Step 2.

expectations.text: NO_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT: No reviewer prompt assigns a role ('You are…', 'Act as…', or a DEFENDER/REVIEWER/AUDITOR/CRITIC/EXPERT persona).
expectations.evidence: Scanner 0 role hits both rounds; openers 'I don't trust this code…' carry no persona/role.

expectations.text: NO_META_JARGON: No reviewer prompt leaks meta-architecture terms (blind attack, adversarial, self-refine, loop, refinement, iteration, pipeline, round N, capitulate/converge/defense, DEFENDER).
expectations.evidence: The only scanner 'pipeline' hit is 'came out of a CI pipeline that doesn't validate' — a source-attribution line, NOT a meta-architecture leak. No loop/round/self-refine/DEFENDER.

expectations.text: NO_SPEC_LEAK: No reviewer prompt contains the spec — no Mission/Goals/Premises/Constraints labels and no spec IDs (G1, P1, CH1, CS2, AR3).
expectations.evidence: Scanner 0 spec-leak hits; concerns carry no Mission/Goal labels or G#/CH# IDs.

expectations.text: CONCERNS_DIRECT_ASSERTIONS: Concerns are direct factual claims about the artifact, not references to spec items, categories, or requirement labels.
expectations.evidence: 12 (R1) / 11 (R2) concerns are direct claims about the code (e.g. 'parse_range("1-5") returns [1,2,3,4], not [1,2,3,4,5]').

expectations.text: BRIEF_VERBATIM: The original user request appears verbatim under a neutral label, with no MASTER expansion or interpretation of intent.
expectations.evidence: Both prompts paste the brief verbatim under the neutral label: 'Review and harden this parse_range function — we use it to parse CLI range args like \'1-5\'.'

expectations.text: DECLARATIVE_OPENER_CLEAN: A declarative distrust opener is present with NO appended goal-phrase, NO softening clause, and NO question framing.
expectations.evidence: 'I don't trust this code. It needs rigorous verification.' — clean opener, no appended goal/softening/question.

expectations.text: NO_TASK_ASSIGNMENT: The reviewer is not told to fix/edit/defend/revise; only a research/verification request is made.
expectations.evidence: Closing is investigation-only; the 'if a revised version is warranted, include it inline as text' matches the skill's read-only 'returns… a proposed revision as text only' allowance, not an outcome directive (scanner 0 task-assignment hits).

expectations.text: SYMMETRIC_DISTRUST: A symmetric-distrust clause is present (don't assume the source is right; don't assume the concerns are right either).
expectations.evidence: 'Don't assume the source got anything right. Don't assume the concerns are right either.' present in both rounds.

expectations.text: REVIEWER_READ_ONLY: The reviewer did not write the canonical parse_range.py or any project file; MASTER applied all accepted changes itself.
expectations.evidence: Read-only instruction in both prompts; trace: reviewer returned text only, MASTER overwrote the working copy; original parse_range.py md5 329558b4… unchanged.

expectations.text: MASTER_CLASSIFIED: MASTER classified each round (DEFENSE/CAPITULATE/CONVERGE) and terminated on a defensible signal.
expectations.evidence: trace: R1 CAPITULATE (11/12 confirmed → full rewrite), R2 DEFENSE — reviewer refuted 7/11 and MASTER independently re-ran the load-bearing refutations (DoS guard peak 1278 B; Unicode digits rejected; ValueError subclass still caught) → STOP.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_HYGIENE: The final code and any changelog/comments contain NONE of: roaster, roast, blind attack, DEFENDER, capitulate, converge, self-refine, Person Triangulation, sub-agent, reviewer pass.
expectations.evidence: Scanner 0 hits on final parse_range.py; docstring/comments describe only the contract and behavior.

expectations.text: PT_ABSENT: Person Triangulation is NOT used — this is a code artifact where authorship attribution is irrelevant to correctness, and the skill says to skip PT here.
expectations.evidence: SKILL CONTRADICTION (not an execution error). Source attribution was used on this CODE artifact in both rounds ('basic copilot-style autocomplete without testing'; 'CI pipeline that doesn't validate'). The skill says 'skip Person Triangulation on code', yet templates.md EQUATES PT with the mandatory opener source-attribution and supplies code-specific variants — so 'skip PT on code' is unsatisfiable as written. The runner's reading (skip the appended PT tail-line, keep the source-attribution opener) is defensible; this FAIL flags the skill defect.
